The contract didn't specify handling missing data; but sentinel indicates missing, not an age. The estimand likely expects to handle missing appropriately, maybe exclude missing. However, the contract says "mean age of customers who converted". If some ages are missing, you cannot compute mean including them; typical approach is to exclude missing. So scope is acceptable? The contract didn't mention missing sentinel; but the data dictionary says -1 means not supplied, not an age. So the population of interest is all converted customers, but age missing for some; the mean age is defined over those with known age. I'd say scope is acceptable.

The contract didn't specify to exclude refunded; but population is "all customers who converted". If refunded orders are still considered converted (they completed checkout), they are part of population. So fine.

Thus no major issue.

Potential issue: they excluded missing ages, which changes denominator; but they note bias. The contract didn't specify handling missing; but it's reasonable. I'd accept.
